card.title: Same Memory, Different Meaning
card.instruction: Return to one shared memory as comfort, then evidence, then accusation, changing its meaning without abandoning the facts.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before my exhibition, I keep thinking how you hung my first painting. It makes me feel safe here.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Still in the hall. I point it out to everyone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So that's proof you believed in me before the reviews.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I tell them even you had to start somewhere.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You hung it to reassure everyone else they couldn't possibly do worse.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 hanging the first painting gives safety, A3 makes it proof of belief and A5 accuses B of using it to reassure others through inferiority.

relationship.evidence: B2 and B4 have plausible supportive display motives which A increasingly mistrusts.

heightening.evidence: B4 reassurance to visitors is reinterpreted at A5 as contempt for A's early ability.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 could not do worse converts B4 benign phrase into a precise accusation.
